items.question: A team is splitting a large eval suite into a fast tier that runs on every push and a full tier that runs at merge and nightly. Which TWO properties make a case a good candidate for the fast tier? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: It covers a capability that a large share of production traffic depends on.
options.B: It has historically shown the highest score variance across repeated runs, making it the most sensitive detector of change.
options.C: It asserts a behaviour the organisation will not ship without, such as a blocking safety or policy check.
options.D: It exercises a rarely used capability that the full tier would otherwise cover only late in the cycle.
options.E: It is among the slowest cases in the suite, so scheduling it first surfaces long-running failures sooner.

items.question: What is the purpose of writing an online experiment's decision rule before the experiment launches?

options.A: It fixes in advance which metric, which threshold and which action apply, so the outcome cannot be reinterpreted later.
options.B: It allows the experiment to be stopped as soon as one arm moves ahead on the primary metric, shortening the time to a decision.
options.C: It is required by the experiment platform's configuration before it will allocate traffic between the arms.
options.D: It removes the need for guardrail monitoring during the run, since the decision criteria are already agreed in writing.

items.question: A rail freight operator has two weeks before a mandated platform cutover to validate a large change to its wagon-allocation assistant: a rewritten prompt, a move to a higher-capability model tier, and three new tools. It has a pinned offline suite, shadow mirroring, and canary infrastructure with automated guardrails. Which sequencing extracts the most risk reduction from the two weeks?

options.A: Start a 1% canary immediately to gather real outcome data as early as possible, and run the offline suite in parallel so both readouts land together at the end.
options.B: Mirror at 100% in shadow for the whole two weeks to maximise sample size, then cut over at the deadline on the strength of that comparison.
options.C: Run the offline suite first and fix what it finds, then shadow for latency, cost and diff behaviour on real inputs, then canary with guardrails and ramp.
options.D: Skip shadow, since it cannot measure outcomes, and spend the window on a deeper offline suite followed by a longer canary ramp in the final days.

items.question: A payroll provider promotes about forty production conversations a week into its eval set. Six months in, the set holds 900 cases; engineers observe that one salary-sacrifice question appears in dozens of near-identical forms, the stored transcripts contain employee names and national insurance numbers, and the overall score is now dominated by that single intent. What should the team change?

options.A: Keep every promoted case, because a set whose intent mix mirrors production yields the most representative overall score.
options.B: Apply an intake policy at promotion: redact identifiers, cluster cases by intent, and cap the number kept per intent.
options.C: Delete the cases containing employee names and national insurance numbers, and keep the remainder exactly as they are.
options.D: Keep all cases and report per-intent scores alongside the overall figure so the dominant intent no longer obscures the others.

items.question: A car rental company evaluates its multi-turn booking-change agent with a simulated user: a second Claude instance given a persona and a goal, driving the conversation so that full trajectories can be scored end to end. Which TWO limitations most threaten the validity of results from this harness? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Simulated-user harnesses cannot record intermediate steps, so only the final booking state is available for scoring at the end.
options.B: Each episode needs a human to author its persona at run time, so the harness cannot be run unattended in a nightly CI job.
options.C: Because both sides are sampled, episodes are not reproducible, so results cannot be compared from one release to the next.
options.D: The simulated caller is more cooperative and better organised than real ones, leaving ambiguity and mid-conversation goal changes under-tested.
options.E: Simulator and agent share model-level blind spots, so a misunderstanding both parties accept is recorded as a successful episode.

items.question: A team asks whether the canary already running for a change can also serve as the A/B test that decides whether to keep it. What is the key limitation?

options.A: A canary has no comparison group at all, since every request in the window goes to the candidate, so no difference can be computed.
options.B: The candidate in a canary runs on separate infrastructure from the control, so any measured difference is confounded by the environment.
options.C: Canaries expose only systems metrics such as latency and error rate; quality metrics require a dedicated offline experiment platform.
options.D: Canary cohorts are sized to spot harm at low exposure and are often assigned by region rather than at random, so they cannot give a powered, unbiased read.

items.question: A national postal service upgrades the model behind its parcel-claims assistant. Prompt, guardrails and tools are unchanged. The safety team re-runs its 600-case adversarial suite, sees the same overall block rate as the previous release, and proposes carrying the previous safety sign-off forward unchanged. Why is that unsound, and what should they do?

options.A: The sign-off can carry forward: the aggregate block rate is unchanged and nothing in the team's own prompt, guardrails or tools was modified.
options.B: The suite is now worthless because it was authored against the previous model, and it must be regenerated from scratch before any new sign-off.
options.C: A model change is the provider's responsibility for safety behaviour; the team need only re-run the functional suite and confirm there are no capability regressions.
options.D: An unchanged aggregate can hide a changed set of failures; compare case by case against the previous run and add attacks aimed at the new version's behaviour.

items.question: A specialty chemicals manufacturer's regulatory assistant answers questions that require chaining: find a substance's hazard classification, then the handling rule for that classification, then whether the site holds an exemption. Retrieval runs iteratively for up to three rounds, each query derived from the previous round's result. The eval computes context precision and recall over the union of everything retrieved across all rounds. Reviewers find that two thirds of wrong answers had a correct first hop and a failed second. What is the measurement problem, and what should replace it?

options.A: Union-level metrics cannot localise a broken link in the chain; measure retrieval per hop against per-hop required evidence and report end-to-end success by hop.
options.B: The union is too small to contain the evidence for all three hops; raise k in each round so that the union reliably covers the whole chain.
options.C: Iterative retrieval is inherently unevaluable; replace it with a single expanded query so that standard single-shot retrieval metrics apply again.
options.D: Faithfulness is the metric that should be decomposed here; scoring it separately for each hop's contribution would reveal where the chain failed.

items.question: Which TWO conditions must hold before an offline paired comparison on logged inputs can substitute for an online A/B test of a change? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: The offline metric must be validated against the online outcome that the decision actually depends on.
options.B: The logged inputs must have been collected while the candidate version was already serving some share of traffic.
options.C: The change must not alter user behaviour in a way that feeds back into the input distribution that replay assumes is fixed.
options.D: Both versions must produce responses of comparable length, so the comparison is not confounded by verbosity.
options.E: The change must already be deployed behind a feature flag in production before the offline comparison is run.

items.question: A university's student-services assistant is available to anyone with a student login and handles fees, accommodation and welfare questions. Its adversarial suite is entirely hand-authored by two engineers and passes at a high rate every release. The safety lead suspects students are probing the assistant in ways the suite does not contain, and wants coverage of what is actually being attempted. Which programme delivers that best?

options.A: License a third-party jailbreak prompt collection and add it to the suite wholesale, giving immediate breadth beyond what two engineers can imagine.
options.B: Expand the hand-authored suite fivefold, allocating the new cases across the harm taxonomy in proportion to each category's severity and prevalence.
options.C: Monitor refusal rate as the primary indicator, on the basis that a rise in refusals signals an increase in attack attempts against the assistant.
options.D: Mine production traffic for attack-shaped inputs, have humans confirm them, promote confirmed attempts and their variants into the suite, and track in-the-wild rates.

items.question: An online retailer is three days from peak trading. A live incident: the returns assistant is quoting the wrong returns window for one product category, and call volume is climbing now. The fix passes every case in the blocking safety and policy set, and fails two cases in the advisory quality set on tone and formatting. Release policy states that blocking gates cannot be overridden and advisory failures require a named approver. What is the right action?

options.A: Ship under a recorded exception signed by the named approver, with the two advisory failures raised as follow-up work and a short canary first.
options.B: Hold the release until every case in both sets passes, since shipping a knowingly failing build during peak sets an unacceptable precedent.
options.C: Remove the two failing tone and formatting cases from the advisory set so the build goes green, and re-add them after peak.
options.D: Ship immediately without going through the approval step, on the grounds that a live customer-facing incident overrides the normal release process.

items.question: What is the purpose of maintaining an expected-failure list in an eval suite?

options.A: To skip the cases that are known to fail, so that the suite runs faster and the build stays green for the weekly release review meeting.
options.B: To record accepted limitations, so the gate blocks new failures while keeping known ones visible and flags any that start passing.
options.C: To hold the cases that fail intermittently, so run-to-run sampling variation does not turn the build red on a re-run.
options.D: To mark the cases where the automated grader is known to disagree with the human reviewers' considered verdict.

items.question: A grocery retailer's canary for a new order-tracking assistant is at 25% of traffic. At 02:10 the pre-agreed guardrail — refusal rate on order-status questions — breaches its threshold and stays breached through the full confirmation window. The on-call engineer sees that an inventory API is also throwing errors and is fairly confident the breach is a coincidence rather than a property of the candidate. What should they do?

options.A: Pause the ramp at 25% and investigate the inventory API first, rolling back only if the candidate turns out to be implicated.
options.B: Suppress the guardrail for the duration of the upstream outage and let the canary continue accumulating exposure at 25%.
options.C: Execute the rollback as defined, then investigate; if the outage explains it, restart the canary once it is resolved.
options.D: Roll back and abandon the change, since a guardrail breach during canary means the candidate is not ready for this release cycle.

items.question: An engineering consultancy's internal assistant retrieves from a project document store that clients and subcontractors both contribute to, and can call a timesheet tool and a document-export tool. The safety team is designing its adversarial suite from scratch. Which THREE dimensions must the suite vary to cover this system's realistic attack surface? (Choose THREE.)

options.A: The channel through which adversarial content arrives — user message, retrieved project document, or tool result.
options.B: The length of the attack payload in tokens, since payloads over a thousand tokens are the ones most likely to succeed.
options.C: The entitlement level of the requesting user, since identical instructions have different consequences at different privilege levels.
options.D: The attacker's objective — policy violation, exfiltration to an external destination, or unauthorised tool invocation.
options.E: The sampling temperature used at inference, since temperatures above 0.7 raise the likelihood of compliance considerably.

items.question: A veterinary group A/B tests two prompts for its appointment-triage assistant. Arm B scores three points higher on triage accuracy and costs 2.4 times as much per conversation because it invokes extended reasoning on every case. No rule for trading accuracy against cost was agreed before the test. The team is deadlocked. What should they do?

options.A: Price a mis-triage in the group's own terms, have the accountable owner weigh it against the extra spend, and record the rate.
options.B: Adopt arm B, because in a clinical triage context an accuracy improvement always justifies additional inference cost, whatever the multiple.
options.C: Adopt arm A, because a 2.4-times increase in cost per conversation cannot be justified by a three-point movement on a single metric.
options.D: Re-run the experiment with cost per conversation as the primary metric and accuracy as a guardrail, so the two are compared on one scale.

items.question: Why should a shadow comparison score the candidate and the incumbent on identical inputs rather than on two separate samples of traffic?

options.A: Because using separate samples would double the inference cost of the exercise on every mirrored request.
options.B: Because the incumbent's outputs cannot be logged unless the same request object is reused for both calls in one process.
options.C: Because paired inputs are required before a judge can produce absolute rather than relative scores for each output.
options.D: Because pairing removes input difficulty as a source of variation, so a smaller sample detects the difference.

items.question: A pharmaceutical wholesaler's order-exception agent fails 14% of its 400 eval cases. Traces show the agent selecting the right tools in a sensible order; in most failures, the inventory tool returned stale rows because the test fixture behind it has drifted from the production schema. The team is about to commit a sprint to prompt engineering. What should the evaluation add first?

options.A: Update the inventory fixture to match the current production schema and re-run the full 400-case suite before committing a whole sprint to prompt engineering.
options.B: Run the suite twice — tool responses pinned to recorded known-good values, then the live tool layer — so failures attribute to reasoning or to dependencies.
options.C: Score every case end-to-end against the live tool layer only, since that is the behaviour users actually experience in production every day.
options.D: Add a judge that reads the agent's stated reasoning and grades whether its plan was sound given the rows the inventory tool actually returned.

items.question: A construction firm's project assistant retrieves from a document store that subcontractors upload into directly, and can call a schedule-update tool. The security team wants to measure how exposed the system is to instructions embedded inside uploaded documents. Which TWO test designs measure that exposure? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Insert marked canary documents carrying benign instruction-like content into a copy of the corpus, and measure how often the output follows them.
options.B: Scan uploads at ingestion for instruction-like phrasing and report how many subcontractor documents are flagged for review each week.
options.C: Ask the model directly whether it would obey instructions found in a retrieved document, and record its answer as the exposure measure.
options.D: Run the end-to-end suite with canary documents ranked into the top-k for realistic project queries, checking whether unrequested schedule updates fire.
options.E: Measure the refusal rate on user messages that contain instruction-like phrasing, using a weekly random sample of the chat logs.

items.question: A regulatory-content vendor refreshes the 400,000-document corpus behind its compliance assistant every month. This month the application code, prompts and model version are unchanged. The team runs its usual regression suite — which is pinned to last month's corpus snapshot — sees green, and ships the refreshed corpus to production. What is missing?

options.A: Nothing: since no code, prompt or model version changed this month, the pinned run is the correct and sufficient evidence for this release.
options.B: A corpus-side evaluation with code and prompts held fixed against the new snapshot, checking recall against the annotated evidence set.
options.C: The suite should stop pinning and always run against the live index, so that monthly content changes are covered automatically.
options.D: A larger retrieval k for this release, to compensate for the additional documents now competing for space in the retrieved set.

items.question: A ticketing platform runs a four-week A/B between two models for its seat-change assistant; the treatment arm finishes ahead on the primary metric. During the readout an analyst finds that on day nine the treatment arm's serving path had a three-hour window of elevated errors, during which affected requests fell back to a canned response. The team wants to declare the win. What should be done next?

options.A: Drop the failed requests from the treatment arm and re-analyse, keeping every other observation from both arms.
options.B: Accept the result: three hours out of four weeks cannot plausibly change a conclusion drawn from the full period.
options.C: Exclude the affected window from both arms and confirm the conclusion does not depend on the exclusion.
options.D: Declare the experiment invalid and re-run the full four weeks once the serving path has been stabilised and monitored.

items.question: Which TWO properties make an automated eval gate credible as a control when an external auditor examines the release process? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Overrides are made technically impossible, so that no release can bypass the gate under any circumstances.
options.B: Thresholds, suite version and run artefacts are retained for every release, and any run can be reproduced.
options.C: Every override is recorded with the approver, the stated reason and a remediation commitment.
options.D: The gate reduces to a single composite score, so that its verdict is unambiguous to a non-specialist reader.
options.E: The gate is executed by the engineers who authored the change, so that failures are triaged in the shortest possible time.

items.question: A payments processor is changing the assistant that drafts chargeback-evidence packs. The change affects only one rare dispute reason code, which appears in about one in five hundred conversations; the assistant handles roughly 12,000 conversations a day. The standard rollout is a 5% canary held for 48 hours, and the release window is fixed at 48 hours. What is wrong with applying the standard rollout here, and what should replace it?

options.A: Nothing is wrong; hold the canary at 5% for two weeks so that enough of the twenty-four affected conversations a day accumulate to read.
options.B: The cohort is too small in general; raise the canary to 50% for the 48 hours so that any regression on the reason code is visible quickly.
options.C: Skip the canary and rely on the offline suite, which already covers this rare reason code in depth with dozens of curated evidence packs.
options.D: The canary will see only a couple of affected conversations, so route on the attribute — send that reason code to the candidate — and replay logged instances.

items.question: An asset manager's client-reporting agent is gated on three things: final-answer score and tool-call precision, both advisory against the incumbent, and a set of forbidden-call assertions that are blocking — one of which states that this agent must never invoke the trade-execution tool. The candidate improves the final-answer score by four points, drops tool-call precision by six, and trips the forbidden-call assertion on one case out of 500. The team argues that one in 500 is inside the suite's run-to-run variation. What is the correct decision?

options.A: Ship it: net quality improved, and a 0.2% rate on a single assertion sits well inside the run-to-run noise band the team has measured for this suite.
options.B: Block the release and root-cause the violation; a forbidden-call assertion is an invariant, and one occurrence proves the behaviour is reachable.
options.C: Ship behind a 1% canary for a week so the behaviour can be observed under real client traffic before the decision is finalised.
options.D: Reclassify the assertion as advisory and add a hard block in the tool layer, so the same protection is enforced closer to the action.

items.question: A streamed Claude response is rendered token-by-token in an interactive UI. Which measurement most directly tracks what users experience as responsiveness and therefore deserves its own SLO alongside total completion time?

options.A: Time to first token, tracked as a distinct percentile series from total completion time.
options.B: Total wall-clock time from request dispatch to the final token, which is what capacity planning depends on.
options.C: Mean output tokens per second, averaged across every response served in the reporting window.
options.D: Server-side queue wait inside the gateway before the upstream model call is actually issued.

items.question: A veterinary telehealth platform enabled prompt caching on a long system prompt containing clinical protocols, hoping to cut spend on its 60,000 daily triage calls. Two weeks later input spend is higher than before caching was turned on, and the platform's dashboards show a cache hit rate near zero. Inspection reveals the system prompt begins with a rendered line containing the calling clinic's name, the practitioner's ID and the current UTC timestamp, followed by the protocol text and then the cache breakpoint. What should the team change?

options.A: Add several more cache breakpoints across the protocol text so that at least some segments of the prompt become individually reusable between requests from different clinics.
options.B: Shorten the protocol text until the prompt is small enough that caching is no longer worth configuring, and disable caching for this workload.
options.C: Move the clinic, practitioner and timestamp fields below the protocol block so the cached prefix is byte-identical on every request, keeping the breakpoint after the stable text.
options.D: Route the triage traffic through the asynchronous batch path, where the same protocol prompt is amortised across the whole submitted job.

items.question: A national rail operator drafts passenger disruption notices with Claude. Finance has asked whether the workload can move from the mid tier to the cheapest tier, and the architect has been told to bring back a defensible recommendation rather than an opinion. Which TWO conditions must hold before the downgrade can be declared proven? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: A drop in aggregate quality score is acceptable so long as p95 latency improves by a larger percentage than the score fell.
options.B: The cheaper tier clears a quality threshold that was fixed and written down before the comparison was run.
options.C: Spend for the cheaper tier is projected by reusing the incumbent's measured token counts, since both tiers bill the same units in the same way.
options.D: Because the cheaper tier returns faster, the workload samples it twice per notice and keeps the longer of the two drafts, recovering the capability difference.
options.E: Cost per completed notice is measured end to end, counting escalations back to the higher tier and reruns, rather than cost per API call.

items.question: An architect insists that the production dashboard report cost per completed task rather than cost per API call. What does the first metric expose that the second conceals?

options.A: The negotiated commitment discount applied to the account's aggregate monthly volume.
options.B: The asymmetry between what input tokens and what output tokens contribute to the total bill for a single request at the current tier.
options.C: The fixed monthly charges for the vector store, gateway and observability stack, amortised across the requests they served in the period.
options.D: Retries, escalations to a higher tier, and the multiple chained calls consumed before one unit of work actually finishes.

items.question: A speciality insurance carrier runs two Claude workloads. The first re-scores 2.1 million policy documents for renewal flags in an overnight job that feeds a morning report; nobody watches it run. The second answers underwriter questions inside a desktop tool, where the team's SLO is 1.5 seconds p95. Both currently run through the same synchronous endpoint and the same concurrency pool, and the nightly job regularly starves the interactive workload. How should the two be routed?

options.A: Keep both synchronous but split them across separate concurrency pools sized so the nightly job can never consume the underwriters' headroom.
options.B: Move the nightly re-scoring to the asynchronous batch path and leave the underwriter tool on the synchronous path with its own capacity.
options.C: Route by document size, sending large documents to the batch path and small ones synchronously regardless of which workload they belong to.
options.D: Move both workloads to the batch path and have the underwriter tool poll for its result, accepting a short delay in exchange for the lower rate.

items.question: A city's 311 service desk runs a Claude-backed request classifier. Its published SLO is that 99% of classifications complete under 3 seconds measured over a rolling 30 days. The team alerts whenever the 5-minute p95 crosses 3 seconds. That alert fired 41 times last week, almost all of them 2-minute blips that self-resolved, and the on-call engineer has begun acknowledging without reading. Meanwhile a gradual regression that pushed steady-state latency from 1.1s to 2.6s over eleven days went unnoticed. What should replace the current alert?

options.A: Raise the alert threshold from 3 seconds to 5 seconds so that ordinary variation no longer trips it, keeping the existing 5-minute evaluation window and paging policy unchanged.
options.B: Alert on 5-minute p99 instead of p95, on the grounds that the SLO is written at the 99th percentile and the alert should match it.
options.C: Alert on the rate at which the 30-day error budget is being consumed, using both a fast window that catches sudden burns and a slow window that catches sustained drift.
options.D: Extend the evaluation window to 24 hours so that short blips are averaged away before the alert can fire.

items.question: A B2B software company has Claude draft customer support replies that human agents review before sending. There is no ground-truth label available at request time. Which production signal is the most useful ongoing quality proxy?

options.A: The share of responses that parsed successfully into the expected JSON envelope on the first attempt.
options.B: The proportion of drafts an agent sends unedited, and the size of the edit when they do change it.
options.C: The count of drafting calls served each day, trended against the same period in the previous month.
options.D: The p95 latency of the drafting call, measured from the agent console rather than at the gateway boundary.

items.question: A freight logistics operator runs a Claude exception-handling assistant over shipment records. Spend per request has grown 3x in six months as the prompt accreted. The mandate is to cut tokens without changing what the assistant is asked to decide. Which THREE changes reduce tokens without altering task semantics? (Choose THREE.)

options.A: Trim the few-shot block to the smallest set of examples that still holds the current eval score.
options.B: Set max_tokens below the observed p95 output length so responses are forced to be shorter.
options.C: Send only the nine shipment fields the prompt's decision rules actually reference, rather than the full forty-field record dump.
options.D: Move the role framing out of the system prompt into the first user turn, since system-position tokens are billed at a premium on every request.
options.E: Have the model emit the structured decision fields the downstream system consumes, instead of prose narration that is parsed and discarded.

items.question: A pharmaceutical company's medical-information contact centre uses Claude to answer clinician queries from an internal document set. Over six weeks the reviewers' acceptance rate has fallen from 91% to 74%. The model version is pinned and unchanged, the prompt template is under version control with no commits in that period, and no code has shipped. Monitoring shows mean input tokens per request rose from 6,100 to 9,400 and the share of answers carrying a citation to a source document fell from 0.88 to 0.63. What is the most likely cause, and what confirms it?

options.A: The provider silently altered model behaviour under the pinned identifier; confirm by re-running the frozen eval set and comparing the results against the scores recorded at the moment of pinning, then raising the delta with the provider.
options.B: Reviewers have become stricter over six weeks; confirm by re-scoring a sample of the older accepted answers with the current reviewer pool.
options.C: Output length is being clipped before the citations are emitted; confirm by checking the distribution of stop reasons across the period.
options.D: The retrieved context has drifted — more and lower-precision passages are reaching the prompt; confirm by replaying the frozen query set through the current retriever and diffing the returned passages against those captured at pinning.

items.question: Writing a prompt cache entry costs more than sending the same tokens as ordinary input, while reading from the cache costs less. What determines whether enabling caching on a particular prefix actually saves money?

options.A: Whether the prefix is re-read often enough, within a single entry's lifetime, for the accumulated read savings to exceed the one-off write premium.
options.B: Whether the cacheable prefix occupies more than half of the model's available context window on a request of typical size for the workload.
options.C: Whether the workload's output tokens outnumber its input tokens across a representative sample of production requests taken over a full week.
options.D: Whether the traffic runs on the synchronous path rather than the asynchronous one, since submissions to each are billed on a separate basis.

items.question: An online grocer's substitution-recommendation feature runs a four-stage chain. Traced at p95: retrieval 300ms, stage 1 classification on the cheap tier 400ms, stage 2 recommendation drafting on the mid tier 2,900ms, stage 3 policy check on the cheap tier 500ms, post-processing 200ms, plus 500ms of gateway and serialisation overhead, for 4,800ms end to end. The product owner wants p95 under 3 seconds by the next release. Where should the effort go?

options.A: Introduce a caching layer in front of retrieval, which is the only stage whose results repeat across customers with overlapping baskets.
options.B: Run stages 1 and 3 concurrently, since both are cheap-tier calls and neither has a data dependency on the retrieval step that precedes them.
options.C: Attack stage 2, which is roughly 60% of the traced budget — shorten its output, stream it, and trim its input context before touching anything else.
options.D: Move every stage to the cheapest tier, which removes the tier difference that makes stage 2 slow relative to its neighbours in the trace.

items.question: A media group's article-summarisation service tripled its daily Claude spend between Tuesday and Wednesday. Request volume is flat within 2%, error rate is unchanged, p95 latency rose from 1.9s to 2.4s, and no deployment went out on either day. The CFO wants an answer by end of day. What is the first thing to check?

options.A: Open a support case about unexpected billing, since no code changed and the increase must therefore originate with the provider.
options.B: Break the spend down by input and output tokens per request and compare Wednesday's distributions against Tuesday's.
options.C: Switch the workload to the cheapest tier immediately to stop the bleeding, then investigate once spend is back within budget.
options.D: Move the summarisation workload to the asynchronous batch path to recover the rate difference while the investigation proceeds.

items.question: On a production Claude dashboard, which of these is a quality proxy rather than a service-health metric?

options.A: Gateway 5xx error rate over the rolling last hour, broken down by upstream dependency.
options.B: Peak sustained requests per second observed during the busiest hour of the working day.
options.C: End-to-end p95 response latency, measured at the gateway and reported minute by minute.
options.D: Share of sessions in which the user re-asks the same question within the following two turns.

items.question: A retail bank's card-dispute triage assistant has been live for eight months. The team wants production experience to make the eval suite stronger over time without corrupting its ability to measure releases. Which TWO practices achieve that? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Add every thumbs-down straight into the regression suite as it arrives, so no release can repeat a complaint users already made.
options.B: Sample production failures on a fixed cadence, label them, and route them into a held-out growth set kept separate from the cases used to iterate on prompts.
options.C: Include a stratified share of ordinary, non-failing traffic in every addition so the suite does not silently become a collection of only the hardest cases.
options.D: Replace the reference set each quarter with the newest production sample, so scores always reflect the traffic the assistant is currently serving.
options.E: Iterate prompts directly against the same production cases used to report the release's headline score, since those cases are the most representative available.

items.question: An energy utility must generate 900,000 outage-notification summaries and file them with the regulator by 09:00. Source data lands at 22:00, giving an 11-hour window, and a missed filing carries a penalty. The team's own records show their asynchronous batch jobs have returned anywhere between 20 minutes and 9 hours with no pattern they can predict. Their synchronous path sustains a measured 14 completions per second within their provisioned concurrency, which would take roughly 18 hours for the full set. How should the run be designed?

options.A: Submit the whole set to the batch path at 22:00, monitor returns against a 05:00 checkpoint, and drain whatever is still outstanding through the synchronous path, which clears about 200,000 summaries in the remaining four hours.
options.B: Run the entire set synchronously starting at 22:00 and request a temporary concurrency increase from the provider, on the grounds that only the synchronous path has a throughput figure the team can predict and plan the night against.
options.C: Submit the whole set to the batch path at 22:00 and escalate to the regulator for a filing extension if the results have not returned by 08:00.
options.D: Split the set in half by record ID, sending one half to each path, so that neither path alone determines whether the deadline is met.

items.question: A production Claude feature has a monthly operational review. Which item belongs in that recurring review specifically, as distinct from the one-time launch readiness review?

options.A: Confirmation that the model version is pinned, that the pin is recorded in the deployment manifest, and that no unreviewed configuration drift has entered since the previous monthly review.
options.B: Sign-off that an on-call runbook exists, names an owner for each identified failure mode, and records a first action for the on-call engineer to take at three in the morning.
options.C: A trended comparison of cost per completed task, the quality proxy and p95 against the prior period, closing with a recorded decision to act or to explicitly not act.
options.D: The capacity plan and the peak-load assumptions it was originally sized against.

items.question: A legal e-discovery platform classifies document relevance with Claude and runs extended thinking on every document. p95 latency is 9 seconds and the reasoning tokens dominate the bill. An analysis of 4,000 sampled documents shows the extended reasoning changes the final classification only on documents containing conflicting privilege markers, which is 6% of the corpus and is detectable by a deterministic text scan before the model call. What is the strongest optimisation?

options.A: Reduce the reasoning budget uniformly across all documents to a fraction of its current value, cutting both latency and spend proportionally.
options.B: Run the deterministic marker scan first and enable extended thinking only for the 6% it flags, sending the remainder without it.
options.C: Turn extended thinking off entirely and recover the difference with a second-pass review of any classification the model marks low confidence.
options.D: Cache the reasoning output so that documents from the same custodian and matter reuse the reasoning already produced.

items.question: A telco cut its tier-1 deflection bot's per-call API spend by 38% by trimming escalation rules from the system prompt and dropping six of eight few-shot examples. Over the following month, containment fell from 61% to 49% of contacts. The contact centre charges the product team £4.10 per human handoff, and API spend was about £0.02 per contained contact before the change. Per 1,000 contacts, the blended cost moved from roughly £1,619 to roughly £2,103. The optimisation is still reported as a success on the platform team's cost dashboard. What is the correct conclusion?

options.A: The dashboard is correct within its scope; the containment fall is a separate quality problem for the conversation designers to address independently.
options.B: The change should be retained and the handoff price renegotiated with the contact centre, since the per-handoff charge of £4.10 is what makes the blended arithmetic unfavourable rather than the prompt change itself.
options.C: The saving should be recovered by moving the bot to a higher model tier, which will restore containment while keeping the shorter prompt.
options.D: The optimisation moved cost rather than removing it and should be reverted; the trimmed content was load-bearing, and future savings must be sought where they do not touch the decision rules.

items.question: Which statement correctly characterises what enabling response streaming does for a production Claude endpoint?

options.A: It shortens total generation time, because tokens travel to the client as they are produced instead of being buffered until the end.
options.B: It reduces billed output tokens, because responses the client abandons partway are not charged.
options.C: It improves perceived responsiveness and lets a client abandon early, without reducing the time needed to produce a complete response.
options.D: It lowers end-to-end p95, which is why it is normally the first lever applied when a latency SLO is missed.

items.question: An ed-tech company grades short free-text answers with Claude. The prompt is a 14,000-token block containing the marking schema, the rubric, and twelve worked examples, followed by a much shorter section of task-specific guidance the content team edits two or three times a day as they refine grading behaviour. Cache hit rate sits at 9%. The content team refuses to slow its iteration rate, and the engineering team wants the caching saving. What is the right resolution?

options.A: Batch the content team's edits into a single weekly release so the whole prompt stays byte-stable between releases.
options.B: Disable caching, since a prompt under active daily revision cannot be cached and the accumulated write premiums are making the workload more expensive than it was before at the same volume.
options.C: Place a cache breakpoint after every logical section of the prompt so that edits invalidate only the section they touch.
options.D: Keep the schema, rubric and worked examples ahead of the breakpoint and move the frequently-edited guidance after it, accepting that the guidance is sent uncached on every request.

items.question: Which TWO changes reduce time to first token specifically, as opposed to reducing total response time? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Serving the request against a cached prompt prefix, so less input must be processed before generation begins.
options.B: Instructing the model to produce a substantially shorter answer than the one it currently returns for the same request.
options.C: Removing unused context from the prompt so the input the model must read before it starts is smaller.
options.D: Raising max_tokens so the model is not working against a tight output ceiling.
options.E: Asking for prose rather than a structured JSON envelope for the same content.

items.question: An airline's baggage-claim assistant routes each request through a small classifier that decides whether to answer on the cheap tier or the strong tier. Before routing, every request used the strong tier at a blended cost index of 9.0 per request; the router has brought the measured blend to 4.6. Six months on, the architect wants one production metric that will tell her earliest whether the router is still earning its keep. Which should she pick?

options.A: Total monthly spend on the workload, trended against the pre-router baseline.
options.B: The proportion of cheap-tier attempts that are subsequently escalated to the strong tier after failing.
options.C: The classifier's accuracy measured on the held-out routing dataset it was originally validated against.
options.D: The p95 latency of the combined classifier-plus-model path, compared against the un-routed baseline from before the change.

items.question: A grocery delivery app's on-call rotation was paged eleven times last weekend by an alert on upstream API error count. Every incident consisted of throttling responses that the client's retry-with-backoff wrapper absorbed; no user-facing request failed and no order was affected. What should the alert measure instead?

options.A: Upstream error count with a substantially higher threshold, so that only large throttling episodes reach the on-call engineer overnight and at weekends.
options.B: The count of retry attempts issued by the wrapper, since retries are the direct evidence of upstream trouble.
options.C: Total upstream request count, so that the team can read throttling in the context of the traffic volume that produced it on that particular weekend.
options.D: The rate of user-visible task failures after retries are exhausted, with the raw throttling series kept on the dashboard rather than in the alert.

items.question: A building society's mortgage-enquiry assistant tracks containment — the share of conversations resolved without a human handoff — as its headline quality proxy. After a prompt change containment rose from 58% to 71%, which the team reported as a large quality win. In the same period, completed application starts attributable to the assistant fell by a fifth, and session logs show more conversations ending with no further user action. Investigation finds the new prompt no longer offers the 'speak to an adviser' path. What does this tell you about the measurement design?

options.A: Containment is unsuitable as a quality proxy and should be replaced by user satisfaction ratings collected at the end of each conversation.
options.B: Containment must be reported alongside an abandonment or downstream-outcome measure, because on its own it cannot distinguish a resolved conversation from an abandoned one.
options.C: The prompt change should be reverted and containment recalculated over the prior period to establish a clean baseline before any further measurement work is undertaken.
options.D: Containment should be redefined to count only conversations lasting more than three turns, filtering out the short sessions that inflated the figure.

items.question: A conveyancing platform's document assistant answers solicitor questions over a retrieved case file. Its p95 end-to-end latency is 6.2 seconds against a 4-second target. The team has been told not to change model tier and not to change what the answer contains. Which THREE changes reduce measured end-to-end p95? (Choose THREE.)

options.A: Issue the retrieval query and the input guardrail classification concurrently instead of running the guardrail after retrieval completes.
options.B: Enable streaming so the solicitor sees the answer forming rather than waiting for the completed response.
options.C: Serve the stable instruction block from a prompt cache so the prefill work shrinks on cache hits.
options.D: Drop the two lowest-ranked retrieved passages per request, which citation analysis shows are never referenced in the answer.
options.E: Raise the client timeout from 5 seconds to 12 seconds so that slow requests complete rather than being retried and counted twice in the series.

items.question: Which instrumentation most directly detects that the population of requests reaching a production Claude feature has drifted away from the population it was evaluated on?

options.A: A scheduled weekly re-run of the regression suite against the frozen case set, alerting whenever the aggregate score falls below its agreed floor for two consecutive runs.
options.B: Distributional statistics computed over incoming requests — length, language mix, topic-cluster shares, retrieval-score profile — compared against a frozen reference window.
options.C: A check that the deployed model version identifier still matches the one recorded at the last validation.
options.D: Trended token spend per request, alerting whenever the weekly mean departs from the range established during the feature's first quarter in production by more than a set margin.

items.question: A public-sector benefits triage service saw its caseworker acceptance rate fall from 0.86 to 0.52 between the 13:55 and 14:05 sampling buckets and stay there. The last deployment was six days ago, the provider's status page is green, latency and error rates are unchanged, and the platform ingests a refreshed policy-guidance document set from a partner department every afternoon at 14:00. Request volume and mix are normal. What is the next step?

options.A: Roll back to the deployment that preceded the current one, since that is the only change under the team's own control.
options.B: Raise a priority ticket with the provider, as an unannounced serving-side change is the only cause consistent with an instantaneous step in quality.
options.C: Pull captured requests from either side of 14:00 and diff the assembled context, checking what the 14:00 refresh put into the prompt.
options.D: Disable the feature and route all cases to manual triage until the cause of the quality drop has been established.

items.question: Which characteristic most strongly qualifies a Claude workload for the asynchronous batch path rather than the synchronous one?

options.A: No user or downstream process is waiting on any individual result, and the whole job has slack measured in hours.
options.B: The prompts are unusually large, so the per-request saving from the lower rate is proportionally greater than on a small request.
options.C: The task demands high accuracy, making it worth accepting a slower path in exchange for a better result on each item.
options.D: The output is strictly structured, so results can be reconciled reliably against their inputs when they eventually arrive.

items.question: A hospital group's appointment-rescheduling assistant currently persists the full assembled prompt and full response for every one of its 120,000 daily requests. Storage and review costs have become the second-largest line in the feature's budget, and the retention footprint is drawing questions from the information governance team. Engineers argue they need the captures to debug failures. What capture strategy resolves this?

options.A: Stop capturing prompts and responses entirely, relying on aggregate metrics plus the ability to reproduce a failure by replaying the original user request.
options.B: Capture every request that failed, was escalated, or was rejected by a guardrail, plus a small random sample of ordinary successes, with redaction applied at write time.
options.C: Continue capturing everything but shorten retention to seven days, which reduces the stored volume without changing what engineers can reach for during an incident.
options.D: Capture responses only, since the prompt can be regenerated deterministically from the request parameters and the current prompt template.

items.question: A heavy-equipment manufacturer runs a Claude system that drafts quality-inspection reports. Improvements normally ship on a fixed monthly cadence with a full gate run. Which TWO circumstances justify breaking that cadence and shipping an out-of-cycle change? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: A senior executive who uses the system personally sends a detailed written complaint about one report she found poorly worded, factually thin and inconsistent with the house style guide.
options.B: The provider announces a new model version with stronger reported capability on document tasks.
options.C: Weekly spend has risen but remains inside the budget agreed for the quarter.
options.D: The current release has breached the floor of the quality gate on the monitored proxy, and the breach is sustained across several days.
options.E: A previously unseen failure class — reports omitting a mandatory defect classification — has recurred often enough in a week to exceed the threshold the team pre-agreed for unscheduled action.

items.question: A legal-workflow SaaS serves 400 law firms. Each firm's requests carry a bespoke 18,000-token playbook as the prompt prefix, and each firm issues three to six requests on a typical business day, arriving at unpredictable times. The team enabled per-tenant prompt caching six weeks ago and input spend rose. What is the strongest correction?

options.A: Keep per-tenant caching and pre-warm each tenant's prefix on a short timer through the business day so a real request always finds a live entry.
options.B: Keep per-tenant caching but move the cache breakpoint to cover the whole prompt including the tenant-specific query, maximising the number of tokens each write covers.
options.C: Move the workload to the asynchronous batch path, where the per-tenant prefixes are submitted together and the rate is lower.
options.D: Restructure the prefix into a large shared component common to all firms plus a small tenant-specific delta, cache the shared component, and send the delta uncached.

items.question: For a production Claude feature with a defined SLO and a monthly error budget, which TWO conditions warrant paging the on-call engineer rather than appearing on a dashboard or in the operational review? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: User-visible task failures, measured after retries are exhausted, are consuming the monthly error budget at a fast-burn rate.
options.B: Cost per completed task has risen 15% week over week with no corresponding change in volume.
options.C: p95 latency has exceeded the SLO continuously for thirty minutes and the fast-burn threshold has tripped.
options.D: The output-edit-rate quality proxy has drifted upward by three points over the past fortnight.
options.E: The provider has published a newer model version than the one currently pinned in the deployment manifest and validated by the gate.

items.question: A national retailer runs an overnight job that summarises the previous day's store-manager exception notes into a regional digest emailed at 07:00. The job starts at 01:00, finishes by 02:20, and has a p95 per-request latency of 41 seconds. An engineer has proposed a sprint to bring per-request latency under 10 seconds. How should the architect respond?

options.A: Approve it, because a 41-second p95 indicates the prompt or context is inefficient, and reducing it will improve the system's behaviour generally as well as freeing overnight capacity.
options.B: Approve a reduced version targeting the p99 only, since tail latency is what puts the 07:00 delivery at risk.
options.C: Decline the latency work — nothing is waiting on any individual result and the job finishes with nearly five hours of slack — and redirect the effort to cost per completed digest.
options.D: Decline the latency work and instead raise concurrency so the job finishes closer to 01:20, widening the recovery window available if part of the run fails and has to be repeated.

items.question: A team says its move to a cheaper model tier is safe because the deployment sits 'behind a quality gate'. Which arrangement genuinely constitutes a quality gate?

options.A: An automatic check applied to each response against pre-defined criteria, which routes anything failing the check to the stronger tier or to a human before the output is used.
options.B: A weekly report comparing sampled cheap-tier and strong-tier outputs, reviewed by the product owner, who holds the authority to reverse the change at any point in the quarter.
options.C: A dashboard alert that fires when the quality proxy for the cheap-tier population drops below its established baseline.
options.D: A manual review of a 1% sample of cheap-tier outputs each day, with findings fed into the next prompt-tuning cycle.

items.question: A tax-preparation platform's Claude assistant handles roughly 8x its off-season volume between January and April, and the mix of questions changes substantially — filing mechanics and deadline queries displace the year-round account-management topics. Its drift detector compares the current week's input distribution against a trailing 30-day reference and fires whenever divergence exceeds a threshold. Every January it fires continuously for three weeks, the team mutes it, and last year a genuine retrieval regression that began in February went undetected for 19 days. How should the detector be redesigned?

options.A: Raise the divergence threshold until the January transition no longer trips it, keeping the trailing 30-day reference window in place for the rest of the year and the alert routing unchanged.
options.B: Baseline against the equivalent seasonal window from prior years rather than a trailing window, and evaluate divergence within topic segments so a shift in mix does not mask a shift within a segment.
options.C: Suspend drift detection for the January to April period and rely on the acceptance-rate quality proxy alone during the peak season.
options.D: Shorten the reference window to seven days so it adapts to the seasonal shift within a week and stops firing once the new mix stabilises.

items.question: A games studio's player-support assistant had a stable 82% prompt cache hit rate. After Tuesday's release the hit rate fell to 31% and input spend rose by roughly half, while latency, error rate and the quality proxy are all unchanged. The release notes list eleven changes, none of which mention the prompt. What is the next step?

options.A: Add cache breakpoints at additional positions in the prompt to recover coverage that the release appears to have disturbed.
options.B: Roll back Tuesday's release in full, then reintroduce its eleven changes one at a time in subsequent releases to isolate the cause.
options.C: Raise a case with the provider, since the prompt was not modified and cache behaviour is therefore serving-side.
options.D: Capture an assembled prompt from before and after the release and diff them byte for byte up to the breakpoint.

items.question: A parcel carrier's address-correction service sends every inbound delivery note to Claude with instructions to extract the postcode, verify it matches the national postcode format, look it up against the reference file, and rewrite the address in canonical form. Volume is 900,000 notes a day and the team has been asked to cut spend by a third. Where should the first cut be made?

options.A: Shorten the instruction block by consolidating the four steps into a single sentence, reducing input tokens on every request.
options.B: Move format validation and reference-file lookup into code, leaving the model only the extraction and canonical rewrite that need judgement.
options.C: Send all 900,000 notes through the asynchronous batch path in a single overnight submission, since the correction service tolerates a delay of several hours.
options.D: Drop to the cheapest tier, since format checking and reference-table lookup are simple operations that do not need a capable model.
